terms.comment: To wage war, bellum gerere; to make war on, bellum īnferre with the dative; to declare war, bellum indīcere, the regular expression (Lewis & Short).

evidence: Lewis & Short s.v. bellum: ante-classical and poetic

phrases.latin: In amōre haec omnia īnsunt vitia: injūriae, suspīciōnēs, inimīcitiae, indūtiae, bellum, pāx rūrsum.
phrases.english: Love has all these troubles in it: wrongs, suspicions, quarrels, truces, war, then peace again.

phrases.latin: Diū adparandum est bellum, ut vincās celerius.
phrases.english: Prepare long for a war, so that you win it sooner.

sources: John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, p. 183, checked against the searchable text of the book (9 November 2026).
